chunks: From him, from Aḥmad al-Barqī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Sārah, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: If some wine touches my garment, may I perform salat (prayer) in it before washing it? He said: There is no harm; indeed, the garment does not intoxicate.

key_terms.أَغْسِلَهُ: I wash it; meaning cleansing the garment before prayer
key_terms.أُصَلِّي: I perform salat (prayer); referring to praying in that garment
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine; the intoxicating substance that came into contact with the garment
key_terms.ثَوْبِي: my garment; the clothing in question for salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; a legal expression indicating permissibility
key_terms.يُسْكِرُ: it intoxicates; the operative rationale mentioned in the hadith

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in clothing that has been touched by wine before washing it?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on performing salat (prayer) in a garment touched by wine before washing it. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام replies that there is no harm, grounding the ruling in the fact that the garment itself does not intoxicate.
